entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-09-24

Today's batch is headlined by the Hermes Desktop live screen streaming launch, the Hermes Agent v0.21.4 release with machine-readable output, and a pair of deep dives on how the Hermes-Claude plugin keeps your credentials safe. Plenty to dig into.

Releases

Hermes Desktop now streams your agent's screen live. @NousResearch and @Teknium announced that Hermes Desktop can live-stream any agent's screen in real time, paired with interactive desktop passthrough so you can visually access the same machine your agent controls. It was the batch's biggest story by a wide margin (~397k views, ~2k likes), with celebratory sentiment framing it as a long-awaited feature finally shipped — @Teknium's "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" captured the mood.

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (released 21 Sep 2026) adds a --format stream-json CLI flag that emits machine-readable JSONL output — a practical upgrade if you're scripting or piping agent output programmatically.

AgentProto v0.20.0 (released 22 Sep 2026) is a new Apache-2.0 TypeScript agent runtime that launched with integrations for 14 agents including Hermes — a standardized new integration path, and a sign of broader multi-agent interoperability efforts.

Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 centers on MCP security hardening via scoped sessions. Paired with Hermes v0.21.4's configurable MCP discovery concurrency, it signals MCP maturing into security-sensitive, load-bearing infrastructure that agent frameworks must now harden and tune — relevant background for any MCP-dependent Hermes setup.

Merged PRs

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 rolled up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, carrying the new --format stream-json flag alongside skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

Community

  • @rlaope delivered the batch's most substantive community-led extension of the Hermes tooling ecosystem: an [oh-my-hermes (OMH)](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-415aecf318f8) update adding Jev-Skills and model routing to hermes-agent workflows, plus a dual open-source drop headlined by jeval for evaluating and visually extracting Jev results.
  • @Teknium was hands-on all day: pushing back on a reported cache issue and demanding reproducible steps, shipping a quick fix in response to user feedback ("fixed lol"), and clarifying that a tool under discussion is built by NousResearch, not Anthropic.
  • Light side commentary: @rlaope called the freshly released Claude Opus 5.5 "crazy" — in the impressive sense — while staying lukewarm on Claude Code.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Watch your agents work. An official walkthrough video and documentation from @tonbistudio cover the new Hermes Desktop live streaming and desktop passthrough (542 likes on the walkthrough).
  • Run Hermes via iMessage. Official guidance walks through running Hermes via iMessage with any model (121 likes, ~13k views).
  • How the Hermes-Claude plugin actually works. Two deep dives unpack the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: the pipeline drives the unmodified official claude CLI with process isolation, tool-inventory mapping, and a one-request admission relay over stream-json transport. Authentication keeps credentials entirely inside the official CLI via claude auth login — the no-API-key-exposed design is the central security property. Well worth a read before wiring your own subscription into Hermes.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Covers Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, which adds a --format stream-json flag to the CLI. The flag emits structured JSONL (one JSON object per line) instead of plain text, enabling reliable parsing in scripts and pipelines. Upgrade paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The release reportedly rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Deep-dive on the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin pipeline: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official claude CLI, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, and approvals. No forked CLI or patched binary is involved. Version requirements: Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 (qualified version). Each request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools/skills disabled so Hermes tool inventory is what the model sees; a one-request admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request and rejects native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Explains authentication for the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials stay entirely with the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login (browser plus pasted code); the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes, or prints credential files, and no API key exists anywhere in the flow. The plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint, and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without exposing values. Status checks are local (claude auth status reads the local credential store in roughly 0.3s), and separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR to point at a dedicated CLI-managed config.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Overview of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub on 18 September 2026. The release focuses on MCP security hardening: sessions are scoped per invocation and requests are authenticated against invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors are added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB, and Azure Cosmos DB along with in-memory and portable filters. The article warns of breaking changes, including deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, an open-source agentic runtime in TypeScript (Apache-2.0, v0.20.0, released 22 September 2026) that provides one interface to start, message, watch, and stop coding agents with quality gates before work lands. It integrates 14 agents per its README, including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode, and Mastra. The project is very early: single-digit GitHub stars, with Tier 2 components labeled alpha scaffolding. Verdict: interesting architecture but early-adopters-only.
